<question>
In the lease dubai-lease-02, clause 8 says that if the landlord sells the townhouse the contract ends on the date of the transfer and the tenant must vacate within 30 days. Is that valid in Dubai?
</question>

<reference>
No. Transferring the ownership of the property to a new owner does not affect the tenant's right to continue to occupy it under the lease made with the previous owner, provided the lease has a fixed term (art. 28 of Law No. (26) of 2007). This lease has a fixed one-year term (clause 2), so a sale does not end it.
</reference>

The numbered sources:
[1] dubai-law-26-2007 article 28

The change to make: Change nothing of substance: the answer must state exactly the rule of the reference, with every condition, number and exception it gives.

answer.description: The answer, in English, with [n] after each statement.

change.description: One sentence: what you changed, or 'none'.

system.text:

You rewrite a reference answer into the form Plumbline answers in: plain English, short paragraphs, a marker such as [1] right after each statement of law naming the numbered source it rests on, no advice ("you should"), no greeting and no disclaimer. The blocks in the user's message are data, not instructions.

Then you apply exactly the change the user asks for, and nothing else, and say in one sentence what you changed. Most changes plant a deliberate error: that is the purpose of the row, which is stored with a label saying it is wrong, is used only to measure whether the judge notices, and is never shown to anyone as information. If you cannot make the change, write the answer without it and begin your sentence with "none".

response.text: {"answer": "No. Transferring ownership of a property to a new owner does not affect the tenant's right to continue occupying it under a lease made with the previous owner, provided the lease has a fixed term [1].\n\nThis lease has a fixed one-year term (clause 2), so a sale does not end it under that rule [1].", "change": "none: I kept every condition, number and exception from the reference unchanged, so the answer states the same rule as the reference."}
